_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: On a new conversation, the file finder stays put when another conversation becomes the most recent. Two conversations: A, {{A_ID}}, in {{DIR_A}}, which holds only-in-a.md, and B in {{DIR_B}}, which holds only-in-b.md; B is the most recently active. Call "make A most recent" renames A until it is the most recently active conversation and then sets {{A_SLUG}} to its final slug. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /new and wait for the message input (data-testid "message-input") to be visible. 2. Open the fuzzy file finder by pressing "p" (lowercase) with the Control modifier, without clicking anything first, and wait up to 10s for its input ".grp-filter" to be visible. 3. ".ff-dir-path" should have exactly the text "{{DIR_B}}". 4. Fill the finder input with "only-in". 5. The first ".grp-row" should contain "only-in-b.md". 6. Call "make A most recent". 7. The page hears of it: the drawer's '.conversation-item[data-conversation-id="{{A_ID}}"]' should come to contain the text "{{A_SLUG}}". 8. The open finder is still where the user is searching: ".ff-dir-path" should still have exactly the text "{{DIR_B}}", the first ".grp-row" should still contain "only-in-b.md", and the finder input should still have the value "only-in". 9. Press Escape. 10. The finder input should be hidden. 11. Press "p" (lowercase) with the Control modifier again. 12. ".ff-dir-path" should come to have exactly the text "{{DIR_A}}" (a fresh open takes the new most recent directory).
